plan: Economic theory suggests bidding exactly at my private value of $9 is the dominant strategy. This means I should bid $9.0 to maximize my expected profit. By bidding my true value, I ensure I only win when the prize is worth more to me than the second-highest bid. This strategy minimizes the risk of overpaying and provides the most rational approach given the single-round nature of this auction.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly one's private value is the dominant strategy in a second-price sealed bid auction. My value is $9, so strategically, I should bid $9. By bidding my true value, I maximize my potential profit - if I win, I'll gain the difference between my value and the second-highest bid, and if I lose, I risk nothing by underbidding. The independent, random nature of values means past rounds don't influence my optimal strategy.
